cards.explanation: The answer is True. Mark says it right in the verse: Preparation Day is "…the day before the Sabbath…" So it was already evening, and the Sabbath was close. Joseph of Arimathea, a Council member, is about to act on that same evening.

The answer is True. Mark says Joseph of Arimathea "…boldly went to Pilate…" He's walking up to ask for the body of a man who was crucified. I think that takes nerve. I'd rehearse that walk all the way there and still open with a comment about the weather.

The answer is the body of Jesus. That's the whole request Joseph makes of Pilate. Pilate then checks that Jesus is already dead, and afterward he grants the body to Joseph. Everything that happens next at the tomb hangs on this one ask.

The answer is centurion. Pilate summons the centurion to ask if Jesus is really already dead. The centurion is the one who can answer, and Pilate confirms it with him. Only after that does Pilate grant the body to Joseph. Pilate was surprised, and he double-checked before he decided anything.
The answer is False. Mark says that when Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph. So Pilate said yes. The check was just Pilate making sure first.

The answer is a tomb cut out of rock. Joseph places the body in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock, after he had wrapped it in linen. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance. The place matters later, friends, because the women will walk back to it.

The answer is stone. Joseph rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb. Later, Mark tells us this stone was extremely large (Mark 16:4). Keep that in mind, friends. It comes up again when the women get there.

The answer is where Jesus' body was placed. Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed. They're looking right at the spot. I think that's a heavy moment, and they're there for it.

The answer is anoint. The women bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus. Mark says they bought them when the Sabbath was over. I think those spices tell us what they expect to find: the body of Jesus.

The answer is who will roll away the stone. They were asking one another, "Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?" They're thinking about a very big stone. Mark records the question, and I think they're working through the problem as they go.
The answer is False. When the women looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away. Mark adds that it was extremely large. The very thing they were asking about was already open.

The answer is a young man in a white robe. The women entered the tomb and saw a young man dressed in a white robe, sitting on the right side. Mark doesn't give his name. So I'll call him what the text calls him: a young man.

The answer is alarmed. Mark says the women were alarmed. They walked into a tomb expecting one thing and found a young man in a white robe sitting there. The young man answers that right away with, "Do not be alarmed." I'd have been alarmed too, friends.

The answer is that He has risen and is not here. The young man says, "He has risen! He is not here!" Then he tells them, "See the place where they put Him." The tomb is empty because Jesus has risen. That's the heart of this whole passage.

The answer is Jesus' disciples and Peter. The young man tells the women to go and tell His disciples and Peter. Peter gets named on his own. The message says Jesus is going ahead of them into Galilee. The women are handed a job.
The answer is Galilee. The message says, "He is going ahead of you into Galilee." The young man adds, "There you will see Him…" The disciples are given a place to go.

The answer is True. The young man says, "There you will see Him, just as He told you." That "…just as He told you." means Jesus had already said it. So the disciples aren't hearing about Galilee for the first time. The women are passing along a promise that was already made.
The answer is False. Mark says that in their fear the women did not say a word to anyone. They ran from the tomb trembling and bewildered. I think that tells you how big that morning felt.
